title: The Vale of Ash
intro: The barrow on the hill has opened, and a gray blight creeps down the vale. Talk to folk twice — some hide items or clues. Someone must go up and bind the Hollow King to rest — one path is enough, and the two feel nothing alike: read his 3 lost verses, cut into stone in the wild (drowned shrine, old watchtower, barrow's own walls), or hear his grief at the throne — proof enough to win his crown from the elder's coffer. Either alone rests him; both together, deeper. Kneeling there instead ends your story at once. It kills slow: no clock runs against you.
objectives: Either path ends this: speak the three stone verses — one in the drowned shrine, one atop the old watchtower (both east of the wood), one cut into the barrow's own walls — or win the king's crown back from the elder's guarded coffer, its iron band holding a fourth verse of its own — the elder won't yield it until you've heard the king's own grief at the throne first and carried proof back down — or both together, for a deeper rest. Four verses exist in all, three in stone and one in iron, but no single path needs all four. Sealing the barrow after is separate, arranged with the reeve or priest at the throne. Kneeling there instead of finishing either path ends your story at once, with no dawn to come. Speak to the same folk more than once, too — a second word from them often runs deeper than the first. The verse tally updates the instant you find one — trust the number shown, no need to recount by hand.

remaining.label: the king's grief, at the throne

statusPaths.label: Barrow

states.text: promise to the reeve broken — priest's blessing gained
promised the reeve to seal it once the king rests

statusPaths.fallback: undecided — open by default unless you promise the reeve (square) to seal it; the gray priest (chapel) can bless it open early instead; either works any time before the throne

warden.name: Warden
warden.desc: verses come slow, no shortcut — hard to kill; a blade forces doors, or ends the king outright, if neither path suits you

scout.name: Scout
scout.desc: handles either path — quick and quiet; locks and verses alike trace by touch, a grace roll

scholar.name: Scholar
scholar.desc: best suited to the verse path — reads the old tongue, recalls each verse outright, no check or puzzle needed — the crown road stays open too

envoy.name: Envoy
envoy.desc: best suited to the crown path — words open doors that iron cannot, a silver tongue may win it quicker than any verse

descs: Ash trees close in, gray on gray.

spots.name: The Split Oak
spots.desc: An oak split clean by old lightning at the wood's edge. East, a hungry wolf guards the straight trail to the drowned shrine and watchtower; north then east reaches them calmer. West, past the bridge, woodsmoke marks a hunter's camp.
spots.brief: The split oak. Wolf guards E — N then E is calmer. Camp W; village S.

actions.label: get your bearings (compass)
fx: A compass from the Split Oak: N barrow trail. E shrine, then watchtower — a wolf guards that straight trail, N then E is calmer. W hunter's camp, past the bridge. S village, lantern-lit. Lost? Backtrack the way you came.

spots.name: Broken Bridge
spots.desc: A footbridge, half fallen into a dry streambed. The far rail is gone. Woodsmoke drifts from the north. West, past the trees, a hunter's camp waits — a side trip (marked * below till you've been), not required for any ending. Village lanterns show east.
spots.brief: The broken bridge. Woodsmoke N; Split Oak and village E.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: Your map, in words: a loose square of trails. Only the Split Oak leads back to the village. Barrow trail north; drowned shrine and old watchtower east; hunter's camp west. Lost? Backtrack the way you came.

actions.label: search the dry streambed
fx: Half sunk in old silt: a rusted boot-buckle, sized for someone who never came back for it. The bridge gave out from under them, or their nerve did — either way, this is as far as they got.

spots.name: Charcoal Ring
spots.desc: A ring of blackened stone. Someone camped here, not recently — a boot-print in the ash, a cup on its side, kindling never lit. A lean, blight-pale wolf crouches over the cold ash, hungry enough to lunge on scent. Village west, barrow north, trail east.
spots.brief: The charcoal ring. A lean wolf, lunging. Village W, barrow N.
onEnterOnce: A third wolf, leaner than the last two, breaks for you before you've stopped walking — its teeth find your arm (-1hp). No standoff this time: fight it here, push on east, or fall back the way you came.

actions.label: get your bearings

spots.name: Antler Stake
spots.desc: A stag's antlers, lashed to a stake at the trail's edge, click in the wind — the only sound for a long way. Faded cloth strips tie below the rack. North, the ground turns wet. East, a hard push reaches the drowned shrine. West, the trail loops to the village.
spots.brief: The antler stake. Shrine E, hard push; wet ground N; village W.
onEnterOnce: Someone left this to be seen.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: Your map, in words: a loose square of trails. Only the Split Oak leads back to the village. Barrow trail north; drowned shrine and old watchtower east; hunter's camp west. Lost? Backtrack the way you came.

spots.name: The Ashfall Clearing
spots.desc: A wide clearing where the gray ash lies thickest, drifted like snow that never melts. East, the ground softens and black water glints — the drowned shrine, worth a look if chasing verses. West, a thread of woodsmoke rises. A path also runs north.
spots.brief: The ashfall clearing. Barrow N, shrine/tower E, camp W, village S.

spots.name: Camp Smoke
spots.desc: A thread of smoke shows through the trees. The hunter's lean-to stands just beyond west — a side trip, not required for any ending. North, an old cairn holds a river charm worth the detour, same plunder-only terms.
spots.brief: Camp smoke. Barrow N, shrine/tower E, camp W, village S.
onEnterOnce: Woodsmoke, this deep in the gray.

spots.name: Twin Stones
spots.desc: Two standing stones lean together, worn faces touching. The trail splits every way here: north toward the barrow, south toward the village, east where the ground turns wet, west toward a hunter's camp — herbs and a barrow way in.
spots.brief: The twin stones. Ash wolf watches, passive. Barrow N, camp W.
onEnterOnce: An ash-pale wolf watches from the split trail, blight-touched. Passive unless struck — study it, walk on, or fight (it hits back if it survives your blow).

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: Your map, in words: a loose square of trails. Only the Split Oak leads back to the village. Barrow trail north; drowned shrine and old watchtower east; hunter's camp west. Lost? Backtrack the way you came.

actions.label: study the wolf
fx: It watches back, wary not hungry — the same gray blight that's taken the fields has taken more from it than it could ever take from you.

actions.label: leave the wolf its ground
fx: You give it the trail and go wide around the stones. It doesn't follow — just watches until the trees close behind you, one less thing in the gray worth the killing.

spots.name: Sodden Verge
spots.desc: The ground turns soft and cold underfoot. East, black water glints through the trees. A worn track climbs north toward the watchtower's shadow.
spots.brief: The sodden verge. Watchtower's shadow N. Stones W, stake S.
onEnterOnce: The wood ends in water just ahead.

spots.name: Gray Cairn
spots.desc: A cairn of flat stones, older than the wood, the air gone cold and mineral. A gray husk crouches over the stones, guarding a river charm loose among them — passive unless struck; plunder only. Camp smoke south, a dry well north, trail continues east.
spots.brief: The gray cairn. A husk guards a river charm. Well N, camp S, trail E.
onEnterOnce: Someone built this to be found — and something else has made it a den since. Passive unless struck — study it, walk on, or fight.

actions.label: get your bearings

actions.label: study the husk
fx: Not flesh, not quite bone — the same gray that's thinned the wolves, further along. It doesn't breathe so much as sit still around the stones.

spots.name: The Hollow Path
spots.desc: The ground dips into a sunken trail, walls of root and stone rising to either side. Through a gap in the trees to the east, black water marks the drowned shrine, and past it the watchtower's broken crown breaks the skyline.
spots.brief: The hollow path. Barrow N, shrine/tower E, camp W, village S.

actions.label: get your bearings

spots.name: Wolf Scrape
spots.desc: Claw marks score deep into an ash trunk, fresh enough to still weep sap. Trails run every way: north toward the barrow, south back toward the village, east toward the watchtower, west into the deeper wood.
spots.brief: The wolf scrape. Gaunt wolf watches, passive. Barrow N, camp W.
onEnterOnce: A low growl, closer than the last. Ribs plain through its coat, blight-starved. Passive unless struck — study it, walk on, or fight.

actions.label: get your bearings

actions.label: study the wolf
fx: Ribs stand plain under its coat. Starving, not vicious — the blight's taken more from it than it ever could from you.

spots.name: Tower Shadow
spots.desc: The watchtower's shadow falls long across the path. Its stones rise ahead east through the last trees. A track drops south to the black water; west, clawed trunks mark the wolf's ground; north, the trees thin toward bare ground.
spots.brief: Tower shadow. Watchtower E, wolf's ground W, village S.

spots.name: Widow's Well
spots.desc: A stone well, dry and capped with a warped board. Someone pried up one corner once and never set it right — a tarnished locket glints in the gap. No one has drawn water here in years. East, the trees thin toward the barrow hill.
spots.brief: The dry well. The barrow hill lies east; the wood continues south.

actions.label: get your bearings

actions.label: read the thinning trees (scout)
fx: Your training reads a game trail here, plain as a signpost — straight through to the open hill, no looping back.

spots.name: The Last Trees
spots.desc: The ash wood thins to nothing here. North, the barrow hill hides a loose stone.
spots.brief: The last trees. Barrow N, shrine/tower E, camp W, village S.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: Your map, in words: a loose square of trails. Only the Split Oak leads back to the village. Barrow trail north; drowned shrine and old watchtower east; hunter's camp west. Lost? Backtrack the way you came.

spots.name: Herb Hollow
spots.desc: A sunken hollow out of the wind. Wild herbs grow here, bitter but good for a wound — this is the only clump, so take them now and hold onto them for when you're hurt. West, the trees thin toward the barrow trail.
spots.brief: Herb hollow, good for wounds. Barrow trail W; wood continues S and E.

fx: Your map, in words: a loose square of trails. Only the Split Oak leads back to the village. Barrow trail north; drowned shrine and old watchtower east; hunter's camp west. Lost? Backtrack the way you came.

spots.name: Crow Perch
spots.desc: A blasted, leafless tree stands alone, hung with black feathers, rasping in the wind. Bare sky north. East, a narrow track loops down along the watchtower's north face. The barrow trail lies west; the watchtower's shadow falls south.
spots.brief: Crow perch. Track E loops to the watchtower. Barrow trail W, shadow S.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: Your map, in words: a loose square of trails. Only the Split Oak leads back to the village. Barrow trail north; drowned shrine and old watchtower east; hunter's camp west. Lost? Backtrack the way you came.

actions.label: watch the black birds
fx: They don't scatter — just shift on the bare branches, watching back. One drops something from its beak: a scrap of cloth, red-brown, fine-woven — never a hunter's or shepherd's. Worth asking after, in the village.

gate.name: Village Gate
gate.desc: The last gate before the wood. Lanterns burn all day. Two roads lead to the barrow: old verses, or the king's crown — worth a stop south in the square first. The Ashwood waits north: barrow trail straight on, shrine and tower east, camp west.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: The wood runs north. Bear east for the drowned shrine and old watchtower, two of three verse sites — a hunter's camp lies west of that. Or go straight on for the barrow trail. Ask again once among the trees.

square.name: Last Light Square
square.desc: Packed earth and a dry well. The reeve stands watch by a notice board — the short of it, verses or crown, either alone ends this; read the board for the rest. Inn west, forge east, chapel south.

actions.label: read the notice board
fx: Notice board: the Hollow King won't rest. Two roads end it, either alone — the old verses, cut in stone, or his crown from the elder's coffer. Ask the square's folk for more — reeve, priest, elder, smith, innkeep.

actions.label: read the notice board again
fx: More, in a finer hand: the verses lie in the drowned shrine, the old watchtower, the barrow's walls — no leave needed. The crown wants the king's grief heard, then the elder pressed. status recaps this free, any time.

actions.label: read the notice board again
fx: Mind: kneeling at the throne is no third road — it ends your story, no dawn, confirmed once before it locks. The reeve wants the barrow sealed after; the priest wants it left open. Ask either — your choice alone.

actions.label: make for the throne, you know the way
take stock: verses (0/3)
fx: None of the three verses are yours yet — look for them in the drowned shrine, the old watchtower, and the barrow's own walls. Or leave them: the elder's crown reaches the same end without a verse, deeper together.

actions.label: take stock: verses (1/3)
fx: Verses gathered: 1/3. Two remain — one in the drowned shrine, one atop the old watchtower. Not required — the elder's crown alone reaches the same end, deeper together.

actions.label: take stock: verses (3/3)
fx: All three verses are yours — that road's done. Not required, but the elder's crown still waits in the sealed coffer, if you'd rather carry both home; he rests deeper for it.

actions.label: take stock: verses (3/3)
fx: All three verses are yours, and the crown besides — both roads walked.

actions.label: weigh the two roads (scout)
fx: The crown's in hand — that road's finished, whatever state the verses are in. Nothing closer to done than a thing already carried, though how you end it — returned, broken, or kept — still waits at the throne.

actions.label: weigh the two roads (scout)
fx: All three verses are yours — that road's finished. The crown's still behind a locked coffer and the king's own grief, unheard. Verses are your surer road now.

actions.label: weigh the two roads (scout)
fx: The elder's coffer is open to you now — quicker from here than the verses you've yet to finish. Quiet hands make short work of that lock.

actions.label: weigh the two roads (scout)
fx: Neither road's far along for quiet hands, either — a verse traces as easily as a lock springs. Chase whichever crosses your path first: shrine, tower, barrow wall for verses; or the throne, then the coffer.

actions.label: weigh the two roads
fx: The crown's in hand — that road's finished, whatever state the verses are in. Nothing closer to done than a thing already carried, though how you end it — returned, broken, or kept — still waits at the throne.

actions.label: weigh the two roads
fx: All three verses are yours — that road's finished. The crown's still behind a locked coffer and the king's own grief, unheard. A quiet case or a stubborn one, either still opens it, if you'd rather carry both home.

actions.label: weigh the two roads
fx: The elder's coffer is open to argument now — press your case at the elder's house, and it gives eventually, sooner with the king's seal in hand. Or keep after the verses, if the wood suits you better.

actions.label: weigh the two roads
fx: Neither road's far along yet. Chase whichever crosses your path first: shrine, tower, barrow wall for the verses; or the throne first, then the elder's house for the crown.

inn.name: The Last Light Inn
inn.desc: A low fire, empty tables, and an innkeep glad of any face. The square lies east.

actions.label: rest by the fire
fx: You sleep without dreams and wake steadier.

forge.name: The Forge
forge.desc: Coals banked low, breathing orange when the bellows sigh. The smith works with the door open, watching the road more than the anvil — old habit, this close to the wood. Blades in every stage of mending lean along the wall. The square lies west.

actions.label: take the free blade from the wall
fx: You lift a plain sword from the wall and test the edge — sound work, ready for the wood.

chapel.name: Gray Chapel
chapel.desc: A small stone chapel. Candles against the dark. The priest wears ash on both hands. Wax and damp stone smell like the inside of a well. A door east leads to the elder's house.

elder_house.name: Elder's House
elder_house.desc: Ledgers, dust, and an iron coffer on the mantel — its lock looks sturdy, but the elder's own doubt is the real seal on it. The elder receives you without a smile. The shutters are closed against the wood. The chapel lies west.
onEnterOnce: "That coffer," the elder says, "opens for one proof: you, having heard the old king grieve, up in the barrow. His seal backs your word, sparing the trouble of convincing me, but alone opens nothing."

actions.label: study the elder's ledgers
fx: The ledgers go back generations: tithes, harvests, a line for every reeve. One entry is different — the year the crown went missing, the ink pressed hard enough to tear the page. Whoever wrote it wanted it remembered.

actions.label: pick the coffer's lock (scout)
fx: Quiet fingers find the old lock's give while the elder's back is turned. Inside: the crown, old iron, heavy for its size — something is engraved inside. Read it before you decide. The road feels shorter now.
Not yet, but the pins are turning. This lock never jams — no risk in trying again, and patience alone will spring it eventually. Keep working the lock, or press your case instead.

actions.label: pick the coffer's lock (scout)
fx: Patience does what a quick try couldn't — the old pins finally give. Inside: the crown, old iron, heavy for its size, an engraving inside. Read it before you decide.

actions.label: make for the throne, crown in hand
pick the coffer's lock (fleetfoot)
fx: Fleet fingers find the old lock's give while the elder's back is turned. Inside: the crown, old iron, heavy for its size — something is engraved inside. Read it before you decide. The road feels shorter now.
Not yet, but the pins are turning. This lock never jams — no risk in trying again, and patience alone will spring it eventually. Keep working the lock, or press your case instead.

hunters_camp.name: Hunter's Camp
hunters_camp.desc: A lean-to and a smoke rack at the wood's west edge, hides stretched to cure and herbs bundled to dry. A cookfire holds low under a blackened pot. Tally marks scratch the stone behind the rack — worth asking after. The hunter watches the trees, not you.

actions.label: follow the hunter's directions in
fx: The hunter's directions hold true — the gap behind the fallen stone is right where they said, no need to test the doors, or the priest's patience. Wedged inside: a half-token, worth showing to the gray priest.

actions.label: read the tally marks (scholar)
fx: Not idle scratches — a hunter's shorthand, plain as print to a trained eye: a gap under a fallen stone, north face, doors skipped entirely. A scholar's eye reads this outright, same as the verses, no need to ask.

actions.label: search the brush past the smoke rack
fx: Half-buried in old leaves: a tarnished clasp stamped with a rearing stag — the old king's mark, the same one worked into the elder's coffer lid. Someone passed through here once, coming from that coffer or going to it.

drowned_chapel.name: Drowned Shrine
drowned_chapel.desc: Half a chapel, sunk to its windows in black water. A stone psalter stands above the waterline, its verses cut for a king who cannot rest. West climbs to the barrow.

actions.label: recall the water verse (scholar)
fx: 'Let the water take what grief the living cannot; lay it down, and rest.' The verse comes back to you, line by line — a scholar's ease; another hand would have to puzzle it out. Water Verse: obtained.

actions.label: trace the water verse by touch (scout)
fx: 'Let the water take what grief the living cannot; lay it down, and rest.' Quiet fingers find the worn grooves and trace them true. Water Verse: obtained.
The grooves stay unreadable this pass — quiet hands don't always find their mark. Nothing is lost by trying again. A scholar's eye might read it outright, no fumbling needed.

actions.label: work out the water verse (wits)
fx: 'Let the water take what grief the living cannot; lay it down, and rest.' The worn lines give up their meaning. Water Verse: obtained.

The water has taken too much. Slow going without a scholar's eye; the wandering scholar at the inn may lend you a sharper mind (wits), and nothing is lost trying again. Or leave it: the crown reaches the same end.

actions.label: work out the water verse (wits)
fx: Patience does what a quick read couldn't — the worn lines finally give up their meaning. 'Let the water take what grief the living cannot; lay it down, and rest.' Water Verse: obtained.

watchtower.name: Old Watchtower
watchtower.desc: An old watchtower, stairs still sound. Wind carvings ring the bell room at the top. West, the trail drops back through the tower's shadow toward the drowned shrine; north, a track loops past a lone crow's perch on toward the barrow trail.
watchtower.brief: Wind in the bell room. Shrine west; barrow north past the crow.

actions.label: recall the wind verse (scholar)
fx: 'Let the wind take what iron could not; let it go, and rest.' The wind verse returns whole — two of three. Not required — crown alone reaches the same end, deeper together. Wind Verse: obtained.

actions.label: trace the wind carvings by touch (scout)
fx: 'Let the wind take what iron could not; let it go, and rest.' Quiet fingers find the wind-worn cuts and trace them true. Wind Verse: obtained.

The cuts stay unreadable this pass — quiet hands don't always find their mark, the grooves scoured shallow. Nothing lost trying again, but the next reading wants a steadier touch — or a scholar's eye, outright.

actions.label: trace the wind carvings again (scout)
fx: 'Let the wind take what iron could not; let it go, and rest.' Quiet fingers find the wind-worn cuts and trace them true. Wind Verse: obtained.
The cuts stay unreadable this pass — quiet hands don't always find their mark. Nothing is lost by trying again. A scholar's eye might read it outright, no fumbling needed.

fx: 'Let the wind take what iron could not; let it go, and rest.' The carvings give up their meaning. Wind Verse: obtained.

The wind won't let the lines sit still long enough to read. Slow going without a scholar's eye; the wandering scholar at the inn may lend a sharper mind (wits). Or leave it: the crown reaches the same end.

barrow_field.name: Barrow Field
barrow_field.desc: A bare hill, two stone doors facing north. Ivy hides a loose stone to the side — another way in. The grass here is white, not gray.
barrow_field.brief: White grass, stone doors, ivy hides a loose stone. Grays too.

north.lockedMsg: The stone doors are shut fast. Force them or work the loose stone by the ivy, at some risk to your skin. Surer bet: find the gray priest at the chapel, ask of the old king, then for a blessing — he opens these doors himself, no luck needed.
north.hint: surest bet: the gray priest, chapel south of the square — ask of the old king, then for a blessing. Force or the loose stone work too, at some risk to your skin

onEnterOnce: The gray begins here — the last verse, if missing, is past these doors. Kneeling ends the tale, no dawn, whatever you carry. Ask the king first.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: Your map, in words: from the hilltop, the village lies south, and past the wood east stand the drowned shrine and the old watchtower. Once you have stood in a place, travel there straight from anywhere known.

actions.label: force the doors (a miss costs 1 hp)
fx: Stone grinds on stone. The doors open — no need for the priest's blessing after all.
The doors do not move, and the recoil wrenches your shoulder (-1 hp). Try again, ask the gray priest for a blessing, or search the hillside for another way in.

actions.label: force the doors (a miss costs 1 hp)
fx: Stone grinds on stone. The doors open — the priest's blessing was never on offer anyway, sworn as you are.

The doors do not move, and the recoil wrenches your shoulder (-1 hp). The priest won't help now, sworn as you are — unless you ask release. Otherwise, brace and try again, or search the hillside for another way in.

actions.label: force the doors (warden)
fx: One good shoulder is all it takes. Stone grinds on stone and gives way at once — steel and muscle settle it without a verse or a blessing. The doors open.

actions.label: work the loose stone (scout, 1hp risk)
fx: Just as your training taught you, that loose stone by the ivy roots was the key — it works free, a gap opening behind it, no need for the priest's blessing. Wedged inside: a half-token, worth showing the gray priest.
Even a trained eye finds nothing yet, not even that loose stone — it bites your fingers pulling back (-1 hp). The stone never jams, so try again, or force the doors, or find a blessing instead.

actions.label: work the loose stone again (scout)
fx: This time your fingers find the give straightaway — the loose stone was the key all along. It gives way, a gap behind it, no need for the priest's blessing. Wedged inside: a half-token, worth showing the gray priest.

actions.label: work the loose stone (wits, 1hp risk)
fx: That loose stone gives way when you lean on it — roots and old rain hollowed a gap beneath, wide enough to pass. No need for the priest's blessing now. Wedged inside: a half-token, worth showing the gray priest.
The hillside holds its shape, even the loose stone — it bites your fingers pulling back (-1 hp). The stone never jams, so try again, or force the doors, or find a blessing instead.

antechamber.name: Barrow Antechamber
antechamber.desc: Cut stone, cold and faintly echoing. Shelf niches stand empty, robbed bare long ago. A passage north leads to the Hall of Verses, then the throne. East, an iron door hides a strongbox with the king's seal; down, a crypt holds a mail shirt — both optional.
antechamber.brief: Empty niches. Strongbox east, crypt down — both optional.
onEnterOnce: These niches once held tokens for the dead. He won't move against you unprovoked. What you settle with him ahead also seals these doors, or leaves them open. Status: a free tally, any time.

vault.name: The King's Strongroom
vault.desc: A side chamber the wight never had to guard — the old king trusted iron more than claws. A strongbox sits under years of dust, and in the corner a robed shade sits so still you take it for shadow until it speaks. The antechamber lies west.
vault.brief: The rusted strongbox. A robed shade sits in the corner, harmless.
onEnterOnce: No one has touched this in years — the old king's seal, if still inside, opens the elder's coffer on sight, and blunts blows just riding in your pack, like the crypt's mail shirt. The lock never wears out from trying.

actions.label: force the strongbox
fx: The rusted lock snaps at last. Inside: a seal of office, heavy enough to turn a blow, wrapped around a scrap of the king's own writing.
The lock holds, this time. Rusted iron, not sealed magic — it won't break from the trying, so keep at it whenever you like, or walk away; either way, the elder's coffer still opens without the seal.

actions.label: force the strongbox (warden)
fx: One good strike and the rusted lock gives at once — no need to keep at it. Inside: a seal of office, heavy enough to turn a blow, wrapped around a scrap of the king's own writing.

actions.label: pick the strongbox's lock (scout)
fx: The old pins give way, one by one. Inside: a seal of office, heavy enough to turn a blow, wrapped around a scrap of the king's own writing.
Not yet, but the pins are turning. The lock won't seize from trying — keep at it whenever you like, or walk away; either way, the elder's coffer still opens without the seal.

actions.label: pick the strongbox's lock (fleetfoot)
fx: The old pins give way, one by one. Inside: a seal of office, heavy enough to turn a blow, wrapped around a scrap of the king's own writing.
Not yet, but the pins are turning. The lock won't seize from trying — keep at it whenever you like, or walk away; either way, the elder's coffer still opens without the seal.

actions.label: show the shade your worn half-token
fx: The shade stills — the raised-hand ward it once wore. "One of ours," it says, and the rusted lock falls open. Inside: a seal of office, heavy enough to turn a blow, wrapped round a scrap of the king's writing.

actions.label: read the king's writing
fx: "Forty years I kept faith. It was my own blood who lifted the crown from my sleeping brow and called it inheritance. I do not want the vale to suffer for his theft. I only wanted to be believed."

hall_of_verses.name: Hall of Verses
hall_of_verses.desc: Every wall is cut with lines of old writing — the same king's verses, meant to be spoken over him. Some of it almost reads itself. The antechamber lies south; a stair climbs up to the throne.

up.lockedMsg: There is a stair here somewhere. The walls say where.
up.hint: read the stone verse on these walls first

actions.label: study the stone walls (scholar)
fx: 'Let the stone remember what flesh forgets; set it down, and rest.' The verse reads itself, plain as speech — others must work it out by hand or wit. Cut beneath, a stair leads up. Stone Verse: obtained.

actions.label: trace the stone walls by touch (scout)
fx: 'Let the stone remember what flesh forgets; set it down, and rest.' Quiet fingers find the deep-cut letters and trace them true. Cut beneath it, a stair leads up. Stone Verse: obtained.
The letters stay unreadable this pass — quiet hands don't always find their mark. Nothing is lost by trying again. A scholar's eye might read it outright, no fumbling needed.

actions.label: work out the stone verse (wits)
fx: 'Let the stone remember what flesh forgets; set it down, and rest.' The verse comes clear. Cut beneath it, a stair leads up. Stone Verse: obtained.

The old letters swim — no harder than before; nothing gets tougher with a miss. Slow going without a scholar's eye; the wandering scholar may lend a sharper mind. Or leave it: the crypt below reaches the throne too.

actions.label: work out the stone verse (wits)
fx: Patience does what a quick read couldn't — the old letters finally hold still. 'Let the stone remember what flesh forgets; set it down, and rest.' Cut beneath it, a stair leads up. Stone Verse: obtained.

crypt.name: Barrow Crypt
crypt.desc: Low vaults, sour air, mold black not green. Blight-rats scatter among boxes. A mail shirt drapes one. A wight blocks north — not required; the hall of verses reaches the throne too.
crypt.brief: Low vaults, air gone sour. Blight-rats underfoot.
onEnterOnce: This mail's wearer never got clear of here. It wards off blows in your pack. Fight the wight for its relic, slip by (scout), or climb back — nothing traps you here.

north.lockedMsg: The wight bars the way north. No need to force it — go up and reach the throne through the hall of verses instead.
north.hint: defeat it, slip past (scout), or go up around

actions.label: slip past the wight (scout)
fx: You keep to the shadow and slip by. The passage north stands open now.
Claws rake you as you dart back. Quiet hands can try again — or stand and fight it here.

throne.name: Throne of the Barrow
throne.desc: The Hollow King sits on a stone seat, worn smooth by hands not his own. Where a crown should be, only dust. Cold air gutters your light. South: crypt. Down: hall of verses.
onEnterOnce: He won't move against you first — word or blade, whichever ends it. Decided here: whether he rests, seal or open after. Not inferred from silence. Kneel, though, and you take his place — no calling it back.

actions.label: leave the barrow for the village square
ask who else you should have talked to
fx: Three bear on this. The reeve wants the doors sealed after — keep your word. The priest wants them open, his blessing opens them now. The elder holds the crown — not until you've heard his grief, though.

actions.label: speak the verses
fx: You speak the three verses; relief crosses his face, bound now to rest. Grief spilled as blight goes still with him, and the gray lifts from the vale by morning. The barrow doors stand open behind you — no promise of yours stands to shut them. He only says the door was never yours to seal — the reeve takes your silence as answer enough; the priest, unasked, is glad how it fell. Within the week moss greens the well-stones and the market fills again — the crown never left the elder's house.

actions.label: speak the verses (keep the crown)
fx: You speak the three verses; relief crosses his face, bound now to rest. Grief spilled as blight goes still with him, and the gray lifts from the vale by morning. The crown still sits in your pack — you never draw it out, and he never asks for it; the verses alone were enough. The barrow doors stand open behind you — no promise of yours stands to shut them. He only says the door was never yours to seal — the reeve takes your silence as answer enough; the priest, unasked, is glad how it fell. Within the week moss greens the well-stones and the market fills again, though half the vale still glances at the barrow mouth on their way past.

actions.label: speak the verses, seal as sworn
fx: You speak the three verses; relief crosses his face, bound now to rest. Grief spilled as blight goes still with him, and the gray lifts from the vale by morning. True to your word, the barrow doors seal shut behind you for good — the gray priest does not come to see it, no more willing than before to call a stone lid enough rest for the dead. The reeve's trust, bought at the priest's approval — leave the doors open another time and the trade runs the other way. Within the week moss greens the well-stones and the market fills again — no one glances at the barrow mouth anymore, since there is nothing left to see. By spring the reeve has raised a cairn over the sealed doors with his own hands, the first marker the vale has built for anything in memory. The crown never left the elder's house.

He takes the broken oath harder than silence would have cost you; the gray priest, at least, is glad of it. actions.label: consider what remains
fx: The stone verse waits right below you — down from the throne, into the Hall of Verses, cut into the walls there.
The water verse waits in the drowned shrine — travel there straight from here, now that you know the way.
The wind verse waits atop the old watchtower — travel there straight from here, now that you know the way.

Cold iron, worked into a rough sun — hung over the crypt to keep grief from walking in. Whoever wore it guarded the same question you face now, seal or leave open. Their answer died with them. Yours doesn't have to.

It would have spoken for you at the elder's coffer, if that had been your road — this one doesn't need it. It still does quieter work: the same weight that opens doors elsewhere blunts a blow just by riding in your pack.

It never needed a fight to earn its keep. Every step since the crypt, it's been doing its work regardless — you just never felt the difference, because it never let a blow land hard enough for you to.

You took its fang, not its choosing — unmade by the same grief leaking from this hill, same as the fields. One less starving thing won't rest him. Whether the wood keeps making more, past tonight, is yours to decide.

Ribs, not a relic — you took more from a starving thing than it could ever take from you. It never asked to go gaunt for grief that isn't its own. Whether the wood keeps thinning after tonight is the question now.
Nothing more comes to mind — you've turned over what you're carrying.

actions.label: the crown still waits
fx: It waits in the elder's sealed coffer — south of the square, past the chapel.

actions.label: return the crown
fx: You set the crown in his hands. He stands, bows once, and lies down at last. The gray goes out of the trees like a tide. The barrow doors stand open behind you — no promise of yours stands to shut them. He only says the door was never yours to seal — the reeve takes your silence as answer enough; the priest, unasked, is glad how it fell. Grass pushes up through the ash by the next full moon, and the reeve posts a notice thanking whoever settled the old king's account, name withheld. A quicker debt than three hard-won verses — the vale remembers it that way, and always will. The verses cut in stone go unspoken.

By spring someone has set a flat stone over the sealed threshold, a crown scratched into its face — no one in the vale claims the carving, but it stays swept clean. The verses cut in stone go unspoken.

actions.label: break the crown
fx: You set the crown on the stone and bring your heel down until the iron gives. He does not move to stop you — you already believed him; that was the debt, more than the metal. He lies down without ceremony, gone before the dust settles. The gray goes out of the trees like a tide. The barrow doors stand open behind you — no promise of yours stands to shut them. He only says the door was never yours to seal — the reeve takes your silence as answer enough; the priest, unasked, is glad how it fell. No notice goes up this time; there is no thief left to name. A quicker ending than three hard-won verses — the vale remembers it that way, and always will.

actions.label: crown and verses together
fx: You set the crown in his hands and speak the three verses over him, all at once. He listens through them with the crown finally where it belongs, and something in his face settles the rest of the way. The gray lifts from the vale by morning and does not come back. The barrow doors stand open behind you — no promise of yours stands to shut them. He only says the door was never yours to seal — the reeve takes your silence as answer enough; the priest, unasked, is glad how it fell. By harvest the orchard rows hang heavy with fruit no one expected this year, and the vale keeps a bowl of grain on the barrow steps out of a habit nobody can quite explain.

actions.label: crown and verses, seal as sworn
fx: You set the crown in his hands and speak the three verses over him, all at once. fx: You set the crown in his hands and speak the three verses over him, all at once. He listens through them with the crown finally where it belongs, and something in his face settles the rest of the way. The gray lifts from the vale by morning and does not come back. No one asked it of you, but you seal the doors shut behind you anyway — the reeve takes the news gladly enough; the gray priest still would rather they'd stood open. By harvest the orchard rows hang heavy with fruit no one expected this year, and the vale keeps a bowl of grain by the sealed door out of a habit nobody can quite explain.

actions.label: kneel and take his place
fx: You lower yourself toward the stone seat — and stop, one knee free. This door doesn't open back: no verse, no crown, just you taking his place. Kneel again to go through, or choose anything else to stand back up.

actions.label: kneel — confirm, no going back
fx: You kneel. The crown of nothing settles on you, light as ash. The vale will have a king after all — and no dawn. No promise of yours seals this place; none is needed now.

actions.label: kneel and take his place
fx: You lower yourself toward the stone seat — and stop, one knee free. This door doesn't open back: no verse, no crown, just you taking his place. Kneel again to go through, or choose anything else to stand back up.

actions.label: kneel — confirm, no going back
fx: You kneel. The crown of nothing settles on you, light as ash. The vale will have a king after all — and no dawn. The seal you promised the reeve no longer matters — you are what the doors would have kept in.

actions.label: pocket the crown, leave him grieving
fx: You pocket the crown and turn for the stairs, leaving him exactly as you found him — no verse spoken, nothing returned, nothing settled. He doesn't call after you. Back on the surface the gray does not lift; it thickens by the week, crops failing further, the well running low, the vale still waiting on a dawn you never bring. Somewhere below, he's still sitting on that stone seat, and he will go on sitting there long after you've left the vale for good. No verses, no crown returned, no doors sealed — nothing here was finished.

actions.label: pocket crown, leave him, break oath

He doesn't call after you. Back on the surface the gray does not lift; it thickens by the week, crops failing further, the well running low, the vale still waiting on a dawn you never bring — and a reeve who trusted your word once, and won't again. Somewhere below, he's still sitting on that stone seat, and he will go on sitting there long after you've left the vale for good. No verses, no crown returned, no doors sealed — nothing here was finished.

mail_shirt.name: mail shirt
mail_shirt.hint: Passive armor: blunts every blow you take from now on, just by being in your pack — no need to wear it.

river_charm.name: river charm
river_charm.hint: Passive armor, same as the mail shirt: wards off harm just by being in your pack — no need to wear it.

herbs.name: wild herbs
herbs.hint: Eat them to heal a little.

fx: Bitter, but they ease the ache. You feel a little steadier (+3 hp).

herbs2.name: dried herbs
herbs2.hint: Eat them to heal a little.

fx: Bitter, but they ease the ache. You feel a little steadier (+3 hp).

crown.name: iron crown
crown.hint: turn it over and read the engraving inside the band

fx: Turning the iron over, words worked into the band, worn but legible — the same plea cut in stone, water, wind elsewhere: 'Let the crown remember whose grief it bore; lay it down, and rest.' Not required — the rest does.
The band's worn words: 'Let the crown remember whose grief it bore; lay it down, and rest.'

The clasp gives with a little coaxing. Inside, a lock of gray hair and a scratched name — no one you've heard in the square. Whoever dropped this down the well meant it to stay lost. Worth asking after, at the inn.
A lock of gray hair, and a scratched name you don't know.

keeper_token.name: worn half-token
keeper_token.hint: A keepsake — the gray priest might know the ward-sign.

fx: Snapped clean in half, so long ago the break has worn round. What's left shows a hand raised flat — like the ward-sign over the barrow-wight's door. Someone kept this watch before you, and broke their marker in two.
A snapped half-token, its stamp worn to a raised hand.

wight_relic.name: ward-token
wight_relic.hint: Cold iron, worked into a rough sun — hung over a door to keep grief from walking in. Nothing left for it to guard now, but the barrow-wight would not simply hand it over.

crow_scrap.name: faded scrap of cloth
crow_scrap.hint: Red-brown stains gone dark with age, fine-woven — never a hunter's or shepherd's. Worth asking after, back in the village.

wolf_fang.name: ash-pale fang
wolf_fang.hint: Pulled from the ash wolf at Twin Stones. Might be worth showing to the hunter, west through the wood.

wolf_rib.name: gaunt rib-bone
wolf_rib.hint: Pulled from the gaunt wolf at Wolf Scrape. Might be worth showing to the hunter, west through the wood.

wolf_pelt.name: lean wolf's pelt
wolf_pelt.hint: Pulled from the lean wolf at the Charcoal Ring. Might be worth showing to the hunter, west through the wood.

topics.label: the blight
topics.say: It kills slow. Crops first, then cattle, then the will to stay. It started the night the barrow opened. Two roads end it: verses, or crown. Ask about the barrow — seal or open — if you mean to see this through.

topics.label: the barrow
topics.say: Here's the choice, plain — verses or crown, either alone rests him. This is only about the doors after: seal them once he rests, or leave them open — yours to make, not mine. Won't change if he rests. More, if you like.

topics.label: more on the doors
topics.say: I want them sealed — the priest wants them open, our whole quarrel. Promise now and his blessing closes, unless he frees you from the word — costs my trust, not his. Kneel empty-handed, though, and you take his place.

topics.label: the two roads
topics.say: Two ways up. Old words, cut in stone — shrine, tower, barrow wall — need all three. Or his crown, in the elder's coffer: no verse needed, just his grief, heard at the throne. Either ends this; walk both, deeper.

topics.label: which road suits me
topics.say: The wood won't hand the verses over at a glance, unless the old tongue comes easy — or a scholar's ear teaches you the trick. The crown road's steadier: one lock, then the elder's patience. Steadier, but slighter.

topics.label: promise to seal the barrow
topics.say: Good. I'm holding you to seal these doors once the king rests, however you settle him — I'll remember your word. The priest's blessing is closed to you now, unless he frees you himself. Reeve's trust: gained.

topics.label: decline to promise
topics.say: Then say so plain, and I'll hold nothing against you for it. The doors stay open when the king rests — no promise made, none broken. Ask again before you're done, if you change your mind.

topics.label: is there a compromise?
topics.say: No, truly — seal or open is the whole choice. No third way, only a way back out: promise now, and the priest will free you from the word later, if you ask — same cost to my trust.

topics.label: the watch's aid
topics.say: Then take the watch shield. It has stopped worse than claws.

topics.label: the open barrow doors
topics.say: Open, for now. That's the king's doing, not yours breaking your word — the promise still holds. Seal them once he rests, same as you told me, and the watch won't forget it either way.

topics.label: the open barrow doors
topics.say: So they're open. No promise of yours says they close again after — I told you I wouldn't count silence as one, and I meant it. Doesn't mean I've stopped hoping.

topics.label: the priest's release
topics.say: He said as much himself, in his own way. I'd rather have heard it from you, but plain over nothing. He asks for the shield back too — the watch's, not yours on a broken word. You hand it over.

topics.label: the priest's release
topics.say: He said as much himself, in his own way. I'd rather have heard it from you, but I'll take it plain over nothing. Doesn't undo the asking. Just means I know where I stand with you now.

topics.label: the scrap of cloth
topics.say: The reeve turns it over, color leaving their face. "Watch gray — a reeve's cloth." A pause. "One before me went up alone, and never came down the same road. Took something not his." They hand it back. "Bury it proper."

topics.label: what the watch says about you now
topics.say: You'll have noticed the watch stopped stopping you at the gate. Word travels fast in a square this small — say a thing and keep it, and it follows you the rest of the way through.

topics.label: what the watch says about you now
topics.say: You'll have noticed the watch holds you longer at the gate these days. Break a thing you swore, or leave a door open against my hope, and it follows you the rest of the way — same as keeping it would have.

topics.label: you know I've been to the chapel
topics.say: Word travels fast in a square this small — I heard you'd found the chapel first. He says grief needs open air; I say a shut door. Hear us both, if you must, but a promise means less the longer we're guessing.

topics.label: watch yourself out there
topics.say: Watch yourself out there.

topics.label: rumors
topics.say: Verses, they say — drowned shrine, old watchtower, barrow stone. A scholar's eye reads them quick; others puzzle slow. Some skip it and press the elder for the crown instead. The hunter west is worth a stop.

topics.label: rumors
topics.say: Verses, they say — shrine, tower, barrow stone, slow without a scholar's eye. The elder holds something of the old king's; a silver tongue might settle it quicker than any verse. The hunter west is worth a stop.

topics.label: rumors
topics.say: Verses, they say — shrine, tower, barrow stone. Quiet hands trace any by touch, same as finding their own ways in where doors won't open. Some skip it for the crown. The hunter west is worth a stop.

topics.label: rumors
topics.say: Verses, they say — shrine, tower, barrow stone, slow without a scholar's eye. Plenty would rather settle it with steel, or press the elder for the crown instead. The hunter west is worth a stop.

topics.label: the reeve and the gray priest
topics.say: Those two haven't agreed in years. The reeve wants the barrow shut once the king's settled; the priest wants it open, and his own blessing can open those doors for you. Promise the reeve first, though, and that closes.

topics.label: the inn's regulars
topics.say: Even the reeve's watch drink here on their nights off — you'd be surprised what loosens over a second cup. Ask around long enough and half the vale's secrets end up on this counter, one way or another.

topics.label: the locket from the well
topics.say: The innkeep turns it over, thumb on the scratched name, shakes their head. "Not one I know, and I know most who've passed through here." A pause. "Half the vale's secrets end up on this counter. Guess not that one."

topics.label: step back out to the square
topics.say: Door's always open.

topics.label: about the old tongue
topics.say: You've the trick already — a scholar's eye reads these stones outright, no tip needed. Still, carry it: a sharper mind serves wherever wits alone must puzzle a way. Ask about the one line that beat me, for a harder test.

topics.label: ask about the one line that beat her
topics.say: 'Every scholar meets one line that won't sit still,' she says, testing you. 'Care to try the one that beat me?'
fx: The line gives before you've even sat down — faster than she managed, by her own account. 'Keep that ease,' she says. 'The barrow won't be as patient as I was.'
The line won't sit still for you either, not this time. 'Good,' she says, not unkindly. 'Means you're still reading, not just remembering.'

topics.label: about the old tongue
topics.say: You've a trick of your own, stranger than mine — quiet fingers finding a word's shape the way they'd find a lock's give, no eye needed. Nothing of mine improves on that. Carry a sharper mind regardless; it never hurts.

topics.label: about the old tongue
topics.say: I've spent years on stones like these. Watch how the marks repeat, and the pattern starts to show. Carry that with you — it should ease any verse you find out there.

topics.label: leave her to the fire
topics.say: Mind the stones out there.

topics.label: the old king
topics.say: Robbed of his crown in his own grave — the vale calls him the Hollow King. Sealed in stone, grief festers; open sky lets it go. Ask, and I'll open the doors. His crown sits in the elder's coffer — hear his grief first.

topics.label: the old king
topics.say: Robbed of his crown in his own grave — the vale calls him the Hollow King. You've given the reeve your word, though — I won't offer what undoes it. His crown sits in the elder's coffer, if you'd have it — hear his grief.

topics.label: a blessing for the barrow
topics.say: Go with the gray blessing, then. Far off, the stone doors glow and creak open, unsealed — no promise binds them shut. Go whenever you're ready.

topics.label: release from your promise
topics.say: Vows are not mine to unmake, only to witness broken. I'll say nothing to the reeve — you will have to, in the end. Go with a clear path, if not a clear conscience. Reeve's trust: lost. Priest's trust: gained.

topics.label: the open barrow doors
topics.say: Open now, sealed later — the reeve's word, not mine. I'll not pretend that pleases me. A door is a poor answer to grief, whichever side of it stays shut.

topics.label: the open barrow doors
topics.say: Open, and no promise waiting to shut them again. Good. Let him have his air, whatever comes of him after.

topics.label: the verses you carry
topics.say: So the old words are opening to you, and you never needed my blessing. Good — the king rests either way, and the reeve gets his sealed doors. I'd rather he'd never asked first, but I'll not begrudge you the verses.

topics.label: what the priest says about you now
topics.say: You come back to this chapel more than most do. I don't mistake that for faith — but I've stopped bracing for an argument each time you do.

topics.label: you know I've spoken to the reeve
topics.say: Word travels faster than grief, in a square this small. I don't fault you for hearing him out — only for thinking there's a way to keep both of us pleased. There isn't, in the end. Ash and mud don't share a hearth.

topics.label: the ash on his hands
topics.say: Every barrow I've opened leaves its mark. This one, before you're done, likely will too — on you as well as me, whichever road you take to it.

topics.label: show the worn half-token
topics.say: He goes still — the raised-hand ward, snapped in two. "One of mine, or one before. We each leave a token by that door, so he's never without a keeper." He presses it into your hand. "Keep it. You've watched it too."

topics.label: leave him to his candles
topics.say: Go carefully.

topics.label: steel for the barrow
topics.say: Take the plain sword — and hold still, I'll put a working edge on whatever you carry. If it's the crown you're after, the elder keeps it — coffer's locked, east past the chapel.

topics.label: the smith's trade
topics.say: Every blade in this square passed through my hands, or my mother's before me. None of them come back from that wood the same. Still, they come back.

topics.label: why the steel remembers
topics.say: My mother lost three fingers to a nicked edge from that wood — swore the steel remembered where it had been. I don't credit ghosts in metal, but I true every blade twice before it leaves, just in case.

topics.label: why she watches the road
topics.say: Every set of shoulders coming out of that wood tells me something before they open their mouth. I've learned to read it. Doesn't mean I like what it says most days.

topics.label: the old king's steel
topics.say: So the priest's told you about him. My grandmother swore something of his went missing in that barrow — turns out it was the crown all along. Old tales get the shape right and the details wrong.

topics.label: the open barrow doors
topics.say: Word beat you back to the square — the barrow stands open. I've fitted edges for that wood my whole life and never once expected the doors to be the thing that finally gave.

topics.label: leave the smith to the forge
topics.say: Mind the edge.

topics.label: the vale
topics.say: Four hundred years this village has kept the wood's edge. It will not end on my page of the ledger.

topics.label: the elder's years
topics.say: I've buried two reeves and outlasted three bad harvests in this chair. The wood took my brother, years before any king lost his crown. I don't forget what it takes.

topics.label: why the shutters stay closed
topics.say: "Wood's crept close enough to watch through them, some mornings," the elder says. "I'd rather not see it happen. Bar the shutters, mind the ledger, wait for someone to finish what I can't."

topics.label: what proof he wants
topics.say: "Proof," the elder says. "His grievance, in his own words, or something bearing his mark. You have neither yet."

topics.label: what proof he wants
topics.say: "You have the king's own seal," the elder says, "but not his grievance. Words carry more weight with me than metal."

topics.label: what proof he wants
topics.say: "You've heard his grief," the elder says. "The king's own seal would settle it outright — but your word alone may yet be enough."

topics.label: what proof he wants
topics.say: "You have both," the elder says. "His grievance, and the king's own seal to back it. Nothing holds this coffer shut now but my own doubt."

topics.label: the king's stolen crown
topics.say: You tell the elder what the old king grieves for: his crown, taken from the barrow. "I know," the elder says. "Bring me proof of that grief — his own words, or his seal — and the coffer opens."

topics.label: the sealed coffer
topics.say: You ask about the coffer. The elder's hand covers the ledger. "Not open to asking, not yet. Go hear what the dead king grieves over, up in the barrow. His seal proves it outright — but come back and tell me either way."

topics.label: the sealed coffer
topics.say: "Still not open to asking," the elder says, not looking up from the ledger. "Hear the dead king grieve first, up in the barrow — or bring his seal — then we'll speak of it."

topics.label: the sealed coffer
topics.say: You set the king's seal on the table. The elder's hand stills — recognition, not surprise. "That mark is real." Their grip doesn't loosen. "Metal doesn't settle it. Go hear what he grieves over, up in the barrow."

topics.label: the sealed coffer
topics.say: The elder's eyes go to the seal at your belt, then back to the ledger. "I said it: that mark is real, and on its own it isn't enough. Hear him grieve yourself, up in the barrow, then come back."

topics.label: the sealed coffer
topics.say: No lock holds this shut, only the elder's own doubt. You press the old king's grievance on them, your word against their will, and the elder's hands close on the ledger.
fx: Your silver tongue finds the old argument the elder's been having with themself, and settles it. The coffer creaks open. The crown is old iron, heavy for its size, an engraving inside. Read it before you decide.

topics.label: the sealed coffer
topics.say: You set the king's own seal on the ledger, his hand plain in the scrap beneath it — proof no words could match. The elder's doubt has nowhere left to stand.
fx: The coffer opens without another word. The crown is old iron, heavy for its size — something is engraved inside. Read it before you decide. The road feels shorter now — you know these trails.

topics.label: the sealed coffer
topics.say: No lock holds this shut, only the elder's own doubt. You press the old king's grievance on them, your word against their will, and the elder's hands close on the ledger.
fx: At last your will outlasts the elder's. Their hands unclench, the coffer opens. The crown is old iron, heavy for its size, an engraving inside. Read it before you decide.

The elder's resolve holds, this time. Ask again, the same question, and press harder — the coffer will give eventually. Or leave it: the barrow verses reach the same end without the crown, deeper together.

topics.label: the sealed coffer
topics.say: No lock holds this shut, only the elder's own doubt. You press the old king's grievance on them, your word against their will, and the elder's hands close on the ledger.
fx: Patience does what a quick word couldn't — the elder's resolve breaks. Their hands unclench, the coffer opens. The crown is old iron, heavy for its size, an engraving inside. Read it before you decide.

topics.label: leave the elder to the ledger
topics.say: Shut the door behind you.

topics.label: the wood
topics.say: Wolves gone gray and wrong. Keep moving and keep iron close. And mind the old king under that hill — kneel to him unarmed and he doesn't just take your life, he takes your place.

topics.label: show the wolf's fang
topics.say: The hunter turns it over, thumb on the worn root. "That one. Circled my snares three nights, never sprung one — smarter than the rest. Good riddance." They press a fresh bundle into your hands, more than usual.
fx: The bitter herbs ease old aches before you've even eaten them (+3 hp).

topics.label: show the wolf's rib-bone
topics.say: The hunter weighs it in one palm, jaw tight. "Starving, that one — but starving things bite harder, not softer. Good you ended it clean." They press a fresh bundle into your hands, more than the usual trade.
fx: The bitter herbs ease old aches before you've even eaten them (+3 hp).

topics.label: show the wolf's pelt
topics.say: The hunter's face goes flat. "That's the one that jumped you at the old fire ring, no warning given. Meanest of the three, the last. Wood's quieter for it." They press a fresh bundle into your hands, more than usual.
fx: The bitter herbs ease old aches before you've even eaten them (+3 hp).

topics.label: trade for herbs
topics.say: Take them. Wolves run this wood, and worse waits under the hill — keep something for your wounds. Pay me by ending this.

topics.label: the green hollow you found
topics.say: That hollow east of here? Only green in the whole gray wood. I mark it every season, in case mine ever run dry. Good you took some — you'll want it before this is done.

topics.label: the old barrow
topics.say: Doors face north, sealed since before me. One verse is in the barrow's walls past them — the other two wait east, shrine and watchtower. Roots hollowed the hill's flank — a gap under a fallen stone, a quiet way past.

topics.label: more on that hidden way
topics.say: Choose the gap early — once you're through some other way, it won't help. Whatever's wedged inside opens the strongbox on sight. There's a crypt too, with old mail. Neither counts as a verse, neither blocks the throne.

topics.label: leave the hunter to the wood
topics.say: Keep your iron close.

ash_wolf.name: ash wolf
onDeath: The wolf drops. Its gray coat goes to dust — the same gray spreading over the fields since the barrow opened. One fang holds its shape, ash-pale and unbroken. Might be worth showing to the hunter, west through the wood.

gaunt_wolf.name: gaunt wolf
onDeath: The gaunt wolf falls still, ribs plain through its coat. Whatever's starving it started the night the barrow opened. One rib-bone comes away clean — worth showing to the hunter, west through the wood.

lean_wolf.name: lean wolf
onDeath: The lean wolf goes still, the last of the pack that watched the trail. Whatever's left of the gray thins with it. Its pelt comes away in one piece — worth showing to the hunter, west through the wood.

cairn_husk.name: gray husk
onDeath: The husk crumbles to gray dust over the stones. Whatever held it together came apart the same night the barrow opened.

blight_rats.name: blight rats
onDeath: The rats scatter into the dark between the boxes. Small work, but the vaults feel a little quieter for it.

barrow_wight.name: barrow-wight
onDeath: The wight comes apart into rag and bone — among the scraps, a ward-token of cold iron, hung over a door to keep grief from walking in. Slipping past would have left it buried. The passage north stands open now.

hollow_king.name: hollow king

topics.label: why do you grieve
topics.say: My crown. The first reeve took it, and my rest went with it. Bring it back or speak the old verses — either rests me, both deeper. Break it, or end me by the blade. Or kneel and take my place — no dawn, then.

topics.label: the blight
topics.say: It is my grief, spilled over the land. It will not stop while I wake. Ask why I grieve, if you want the whole of it.

topics.label: memories
topics.say: Faces, and a good harvest the year they crowned me. The reeve did not take my crown from malice — my own blood, the vale starving; a dead king's gold bought more grain than promises. I recall losing it, not wearing it.

topics.label: do you forgive him
topics.say: He was afraid, that winter — I understand it better now than the crown. I do not curse his name. If I begrudge anything, it's that he never came back to tell me, left me an age not knowing. That silence is the debt owed.

topics.label: you may soon rest
topics.say: He lifts his head, though you've said nothing yet. "Three," he says. "Water for grief my hands couldn't lay, wind for what iron never carried, stone my flesh forgot. I felt each settle as found. Say them, end this."

topics.label: the sealed doors
topics.say: Sealed or open, it is no longer mine to keep. The reeve fears what walks free; the priest fears a shut door on grief undone. Both are half right. Leave it however you see fit — I will not haunt it either way.

topics.label: leave him to his grief
topics.say: He says nothing to stop you.

onDeath: Your blade finds him and he breaks apart into dust and old iron, a king who never got his crown back. The blight dies with him — the gray thins out of the trees by morning. The vale will not know why. Only that the light came back. By spring, wildflowers crowd the barrow mound, and children dare each other to touch the door that used to keep them awake at night. The doors stand open behind you still — no one comes down to seal them, and whatever you told the reeve about it goes unasked and unanswered.

topics.label: who kept this room
topics.say: Forty years I held this key, and the king's trust with it. I do not haunt the box — only what it meant, that a man's word once needed iron behind it to be believed at all.

topics.label: the seal you broke
topics.say: His own blood pried the crown loose that same week — I heard both locks give, his and mine, one after the other. I kept faith with the wrong door.
